pr.title: Ask the person questions through project question
pr.head: 3f6fbe23aaeb0f1562b091d7dbd81a394b5c8f8c

summary: When a review or fix loop's subagent needs a decision from you, today it can only hand the question to the main loop, which asks it as a line in the transcript. That line scrolls away, nothing lists what is still open, and your answer has no route back to the subagent that asked. The questions plan fixes this in two pull requests. This first one adds the host-neutral part: a project question command that any host can run, whether that host is Claude Code, Codex, or a runner such as Paseo.

1. An agent asks. project question ask checks a one-line question and its recommended answer, numbers it, writes it to the session's store, and prints a reference such as #337.3 at once, so the agent keeps working.
  2. You answer. project question answer '#337.3.a' records the answer from any terminal. Without --session, it finds the one session that holds the reference.
  3. One deliverer sends it. watch, or a view such as the band in the next pull request, claims the recorded answer with a random token, sends it to the agent, and marks it delivered. A claim that goes a minute without renewal lapses, so a deliverer that stopped strands nothing.

The first review found two defects, and both are fixed at this head. A short reference such as #271.1 could name pull request #271 in two repositories, so the second question overwrote the first. Now a session records its repository on its first ask, and only that repository's pull requests take the short form. watch marked an answer delivered before printing it, so a failed print lost the answer. Now it prints first, and a failed print leaves only a claim that lapses.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Session: the id of the agent session that asked, from --session or PROJECTOR_SESSION. Each session has its own directory of questions.
  • Reference: a question's fixed name. #337.3 is the third question about #337 in the session's repository, the one its first ask from a checkout recorded, owner/repo#337.3 names another repository's pull request, and q2 is the session's second question about no pull request.
  • Letter: an answer's suffix. a is always the recommendation, the other options follow, and the last letter is a typed answer given with --text.
  • Claim: a token a deliverer holds while it sends an answer. Only that token renews the claim, marks the answer delivered, or reopens the question.

cards.title: Exit codes the commands add meanings to
cards.html:
CodeWhen
65A check fails, the question is already answered, the answer is already claimed or delivered, or the token is wrong
66The reference names no question
67Without a session, the reference names questions in more than one session

groups.title: The question store
groups.kicker: Questions, answers, and claims as JSON files under a per-session lock
intro: questions.py holds everything the commands do. Each session's questions live under $XDG_STATE_HOME/projector/questions/<session>/, one JSON file per question, named after its URL-quoted reference. Beside them, counts.json holds the last number given in each count, and session.json holds the session's repository.

Every write takes the session's lock and lands by renaming a temporary file into place. The lock is the operating system's exclusive lock on the directory's .lock file: flock on Linux and macOS, msvcrt.locking on Windows. The system releases it when its holder exits, so a command that crashes while holding it blocks nobody, and a command that finds it held retries for 5 seconds, then exits 65. Each answer, dismissal, claim, and settlement is a read-change-write under that lock, in update.

checks.text: The test suite passes at this head, run with Python 3.12, including the tests for both fixes in tests/test_questions.py.

files.note: New module: the store and its lock, numbering and references, the checks, answers and claims, retention, watch's pass, and finding references in prompt text.

checks.text: IN_TEXT finds references in prose. A reference must not touch a letter, digit, /, #, or . on its left. A trailing . ends it only before a space or the end of the text, so Go with #337.3.b. matches and #337.3.4 does not.
try_lock and unlock have one definition per platform. The Windows pair seeks to byte 0 before each call, because msvcrt.locking locks bytes from the file's current position.

Each locked call opens its own descriptor, so threads in one process exclude each other as processes do, and every exit path releases the lock and closes the descriptor. In a scratch state directory, twenty ask processes started at once got twenty distinct references. Of six concurrent answer processes, one recorded, and of six concurrent claim processes, one took the claim.

session_repo records the repository of the first checkout the session asks from, under the lock, and later asks compare against it. Asking about acme/app#271 from an acme/app checkout, then about octo/web#271 and acme/app#271 from an octo/web checkout, printed #271.1, octo/web#271.1, and #271.2 in a scratch state directory, and all three stayed in the store.
The count is written before the question, so a write cut short between the two skips a number instead of handing the next question the same reference.

A claim lapses once it goes CLAIM_EXPIRES_MS (one minute) without renewal. A renewal, delivered, or reopen checks only the token, so a lapsed claim that nobody replaced still works for its holder. The plan and docs/cli.md now say so.

Retention runs whenever an answer is marked delivered. It keeps the 100 most recently delivered questions and never touches open or undelivered ones. Counts never go back, so a pruned reference is never reused.

deliver_pass sends each line before it marks the answer delivered. A watch whose output pipe had lost its reader exited on BrokenPipeError, and list then showed the answer as delivering, a claim that lapses for the next deliverer, not as delivered.

groups.title: The project question command
groups.kicker: Ten subcommands that map flags onto the store
intro: cli.py adds the question parser and run_question, which dispatches before the CLI looks for a projects directory, so the command works outside any repository. ask, watch, and context need a session. list, show, answer, and dismiss work without one, which is how you answer from a terminal.

files.note: The parser for each subcommand and the code that runs them; ask passes the current checkout's repository, which becomes the session's repository on its first ask.

checks.text: watch passes deliver_pass a send that prints and flushes each line. With --json each line is one JSON object, so a watcher reads one event a line. --interval refuses anything but a positive number of seconds.

files.note: Each subcommand against a temporary state directory and a temporary checkout whose origin is acme/app.
